observation_summary: The StringUtils methods (containsAny, containsNone, indexOfAny, etc.) fail to correctly handle Unicode supplementary characters (which are represented as surrogate pairs in Java). When these methods encounter a high surrogate, they treat it as a single character, leading to incorrect matching results when the supplementary character is part of the input.
hypothesis: The existing algorithms for searching characters in strings iterate through the string character-by-character without accounting for the fact that supplementary characters consist of two 16-bit char values (a high surrogate followed by a low surrogate). The logic needs to be updated to detect high surrogates and verify the subsequent low surrogate to correctly identify the full supplementary character.
prediction: The code will be updated to check if a character is a high surrogate using Character.isHighSurrogate(ch). If it is, the algorithm will perform an additional check on the next character (the low surrogate) to ensure the full supplementary character is matched correctly before returning a result.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff shows that the logic inside the loops for searching characters was rewritten to include conditional checks for high surrogates and their corresponding low surrogates. This confirms that the original algorithm was insufficient for handling multi-char Unicode representations.
reasoning_summary: The defect is an algorithmic failure where the procedure for searching characters in a string did not account for the multi-char nature of Unicode supplementary characters. The fix involves rewriting the search logic to correctly handle surrogate pairs, which is a classic algorithmic/procedural correction rather than a simple missing guard or a wrong constant assignment.
evidence_used: The bug report explicitly states that StringUtils methods do not handle Unicode 2.0+ supplementary characters correctly.
The fix diff shows significant changes to the loop structures in multiple methods (containsAny, containsNone, etc.) to add logic for checking surrogate pairs.
The failing tests demonstrate that the methods return incorrect results when supplementary characters are involved.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds checks, these are not simple validation guards; they are integral parts of the search algorithm's logic to correctly identify multi-char sequences.
This is a local procedural correction within existing methods, not a design-level capability omission.
